scope: Packaged Android ARM64 and iOS ARM64 simulator C++/Blueprint Direct data maps; local Mac dedicated Server.
limitations: Development packages; no Shipping size baseline or incremental RTC size measurement.
Authenticated development HTTP only. Android uses adb reverse for signaling and normal network ICE for data; iOS simulator uses loopback ICE.
HTTPS, forced TURN, mobile reconnect, network loss, foreground/background, and packaged mobile backpressure/reliability matrix remain open.
Native ordering/reliability and negotiated-limit fixtures are separate from the packaged shared-API sample checks.
Physical iOS testing is deferred; its rebuilt library has compile/link evidence only.
Native builds reuse existing compiled output directories; these are not new repeat-build or independent-host acceptance runs.
M1 and the external M0 acceptance gates remain open.

source_note: The Server and simulator builds precede a one-line const-reference fix in the Direct automation test. Runtime plugin code and native bridge are unchanged. Android packages and the final Unreal test run include that correction.

fixed_attempts.reason: The first Galaxy C++ message case passed but Unreal truncated the JSON log line. The runner now reads the complete report from that app’s scoped saved directory.
NDK treats a range-loop FString copy in an existing contract test as an error. Changed the loop variable to a const reference and rebuilt both Android profiles.
The fresh native NDK extraction omitted its archive receipt. The builder now writes and verifies it; all cached files were checked before restoring the receipt.
Host-side absolute simulator credential paths were remapped by Unreal. The runner now uses paths relative to the iOS private Library directory.
The C++ message case passed, then cleanup raced the successful app exit. Cleanup now verifies process disappearance even if simctl reports nothing to terminate.
